subject: Hands-on prompt lab + load test windows — scheduling & prep
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Cc: David Nguyen <david.nguyen@acme-retail.com>, it_ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt lab and load test planning

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking the call last week. We're excited to get the POC kickoff on the calendar — the team would really value a hands-on prompt review session where we can walk through our prompt inventory, validate structured output requirements, and run a small load test to gauge throughput.

Quick context: Acme plans to route product search and category tagging through the model. We'll likely want a 2-hour workshop with the Redwood engineers and one 2-hour load test window where we can push realistic traffic. Our preferred week is June 7–11, but we're flexible if you have constraints.

Can you propose 2–3 slot options and the prep checklist? Also please let us know what format you want the prompt inventory in — I can attach our current CSV.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
Director, AI Integrations — Acme Retail
attachments: (will attach prompt inventory in follow-up)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt lab and load test planning

Hi Emma — great to hear, and thanks for the context. Happy to coordinate.

Proposed plan (high level):
- 2-hour hands-on prompt lab (prompt inventory review, routing patterns, structured output templates, and guardrail alignment)
- 2-hour load test (burst + steady-state windows, monitoring and fallback checks)
- Pre-read: our suggested structured-output template and a short list of guardrail patterns

Slots we can offer (Pacific time):
- Option A: Tue June 8, 10:00–12:00 PT (lab) + Thu June 10, 09:00–11:00 PT (load test)
- Option B: Wed June 9, 13:00–15:00 PT (lab) + Fri June 11, 13:00–15:00 PT (load test)
- Option C: Mon June 7, 15:00–17:00 PT (lab) + Tue June 8, 15:00–17:00 PT (load test)

Prep checklist (what we need from your side):
1) Prompt inventory CSV (columns: prompt_id, feature, intent, example_input, expected_output_format, max_tokens)
2) Representative traffic profile for load test (QPS, payload sizes, peak distribution)
3) Any structured output schema examples (JSON Schema or sample rows)
4) Security contacts for pre-load test checks (SOC2/PCI notes if applicable)

We can run the workshop with Karthik as prompts lead and Ben supporting ops/load tests. If those names work I'll send a calendar invite and an editable Drive folder for the inventory.

Would you prefer we run the lab in Zoom or Google Meet?

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — demo + POC team
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Cc: David Nguyen <david.nguyen@acme-retail.com>, it_ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt lab and load test planning

Monica — thanks, that looks good. Option A (Tue 6/8 lab + Thu 6/10 load test) works best for our engineers.

I've attached our prompt inventory (Acme_prompt_inventory_v2.csv) and a short traffic snapshot. David will coordinate with your ops on firewall/IP allowlist if needed.

We prefer Google Meet. Please put Karthik and Ben on the invite; Laura from our product team will join as well (cc'd on the calendar invite).

Also: a couple quick notes on structured output — our product expects a JSON array with fields [sku, category_id, confidence, normalized_title]. We'll share the JSON Schema in a follow-up if helpful.

Attachments: Acme_prompt_inventory_v2.csv (CSV, 92KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt lab and load test planning

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Emma — got the CSV and traffic snapshot. I've scheduled the sessions as Option A and shared calendar invites (RDW-POC-schedule.ics). Invite details below and a few operational notes.

Calendar invites (Google Meet links included):
- Hands-on Prompt Lab: Tue, Jun 8, 2027 — 10:00–12:00 PT (Monica, Karthik, Ben; Emma, David, Laura from Acme)
- Load Test Window: Thu, Jun 10, 2027 — 09:00–11:00 PT (Ben leading ops; we will do a 15-min warmup, 60-min steady state, 30-min cooldown)

Operational checklist we completed / outstanding items:
- We created a shared Drive folder and uploaded the Redwood structured-output template: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcdExamplePromptInventory
- Please add a sample JSON Schema file to the Drive before EOD Mon Jun 7 — that will let Karthik pre-author any output validators
- IP allowlist: Ben to work with your IT. Ben, can you share Salted IP block ranges and a short pre-check doc?
- Load limits: we'll start at 20 QPS for the warmup and target 100 QPS steady state unless you request a different profile. Confirm if 100 QPS is realistic.
- Fallback policy: we'll demo automatic routing to a smaller quantized variant if latency > 500ms for > 30s — confirm acceptance.

Attachments in this thread: RDW-POC-schedule.ics, security-questionnaire.pdf (for Acme's compliance team).

If anything changes, reply-all and we'll re-slot. Looking forward to it.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: David Nguyen <david.nguyen@acme-retail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt lab and load test planning

Thanks — confirmed on our side and calendar invites accepted. Ben, we'll share our allowlist IPs by EOD Thu (June 3). One ask: during the load test can you toggle the routing fallback in a canary for 10 mins so we can validate behavior when a variant is served?

Appreciate the thorough checklist. See you on Tue.

-David
David Nguyen
Platform Engineering — Acme Retail
